extracted.intended_audience: general public and researchers interested in the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation and its grantmaking/policy activity
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation's grantmaking policies, program priorities, transparency practices, and program-specific request-for-proposal/grant conditions as reflected in the page's references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation Open Access Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation Open Access Policy; described on the page as the foundation announcing “world's strongest policy on open access research.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the foundation requires/strongly encourages open access publication of research it funds; references to Gates Open Research and commentary (e.g., Nature article questioning the preprint-centric policy) show an explicit institutional policy on open access and preferred publication platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gates Open Research (open publishing platform)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gates Open Research — a platform associated with the foundation for rapid publication of research outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform promoted by the foundation as a channel for grantees to rapidly publish results; tied to the foundation's open-access policy and contrasted with other open platforms (e.g., Wellcome Open Research).

rubrics_metrics.name: How We Work – Grantmaking (foundation grantmaking approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: "How We Work – Grantmaking" — the foundation's published description of its grantmaking processes and principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represents the foundation's overarching guidance for how it selects, manages, and oversees grants (referenced as a source for understanding grantmaking norms and expectations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grand Challenges / Request for Proposals and Grant Conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: References to "Grand Challenges Explorations (Round 6 and 7) – Request for proposals, grant conditions" and related Grand Challenges materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates formal RFPs and defined grant conditions are used for Grand Challenges funding rounds; applicants must follow program-specific application rules and grant terms described in the RFP and grant documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinvent the Toilet Challenge — Program and Technical Guides
rubrics_metrics.description: Reinvent the Toilet Challenge, Delhi, India – Program and Technical Guides; "Reinvent the Toilet Challenge (RTTC, Round 1 and 2) ... Request for proposals, grant conditions, Seattle exhibition fair program and exhibitor guide."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanitation-specific program documents set technical specifications, program strategy, RFP requirements, and grant conditions for funded projects (technical/design expectations and reporting requirements embedded in guides).

rubrics_metrics.name: Water, Sanitation & Hygiene (WASH) Strategy and Portfolio Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: "Water, Sanitation & Hygiene Strategy Overview" and "Building demand for sanitation – a 2015 portfolio update and overview" cited as foundation strategy documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These strategy/portfolio documents articulate program priorities, desired outcomes, and guide selection/prioritization of sanitation/WASH grants—implying criteria such as alignment with strategy, scalability, technology fit, and expected impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and Reporting (IATI, OECD, financial statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: References to the International Aid Transparency Initiative, IATI Registry, DAC 5 Digit Sector (IATI Standard), OECD Development Co-operation Profiles, and the foundation's Consolidated Financial Statements (KPMG).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows a requirement/expectation for publishing grant and financial data to transparency registries and reporting to international development classification systems; implies grant recipients and the foundation adhere to external transparency/reporting norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic Programmatic Focus Areas (eligibility/prioritization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple program areas repeatedly referenced: global health (vaccines, TB, HIV, neglected tropical diseases), sanitation, agriculture, financial inclusion, education (K‑12 and higher education scholarships), libraries, and emergency response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation demonstrates clear thematic priorities; applicants/projects are effectively evaluated against fit with these strategic areas and the foundation’s stated program goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships, Coalitions, and Public–Private Collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations showing the foundation contributes via and to coalitions and partnerships (e.g., GAVI, WHO, vaccine coalitions, partnerships with Pfizer, Mercy Corps, Save the Children, research institutions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding strategy emphasizes collaboration with multilateral organizations, governments, NGOs, and private partners; grant proposals that enable or leverage such partnerships are aligned with foundation practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for Innovation and Technology-Driven Solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence in references to Grand Challenges, Reinvent the Toilet, Next-Gen Condom topic, Omni-Processor landscaping and technology-focused grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foundation-funded programs often prioritize innovative, technology-centric solutions to development problems; RFPs and program guides set technical expectations and reward novelty/engineering solutions suited for scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring, Evaluation and Use of External Reviews/Consultancies
rubrics_metrics.description: References to progress reports (e.g., "Improving our Work with You: A Progress Report"), commissioned consultancy reports (Synapse Dewatering Investigation; Omni-Processor Landscaping Project), and portfolio overviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation expects measurement of outcomes, uses external consultants and evaluations to assess projects, and publishes progress reports—indicating M&E and accountability are part of grant conditions and evaluation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-limited/Spend-Down Governance and Trust Arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: References: "Gates Foundation Announces That It Doesn't Plan to Operate Forever", "About the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation Trust", and holdings/trust maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governance choices (e.g., planned lifespan and trust management) influence spending strategies and long-term grantmaking commitments; applicants should be aware funding horizons and trust governance implications for program sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Program Databases and Public Grant Records
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentions of the foundation's grant database (e.g., "How we work, grant database (grant for UKZN)") and specific grant IDs (INV‑006827, OPP1152680, Inv‑059287).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foundation publishes searchable grant records and identifiers; these records provide precedent and detail grant conditions, recipients, amounts, and are used for transparency, benchmarking, and applicant due diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement in Policy and Education Reform Funding
rubrics_metrics.description: References to grants and efforts aimed at influencing state and national education policy, investments in K‑12 reforms, higher-education scholarships, and support for journalism to shape national conversations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation funds policy-oriented work and advocacy in education and related sectors; proposals should account for political/contextual considerations and often include policy engagement or systems-change components.
